original.description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. The activity shall establish the required material datasets, perform dedicated measurement and characterisationcampaigns, and integrate the resulting data into an open-access database supporting DQS compliance assessments and brightness prediction tools. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 7.

original.description: ObjectivesTo develop a low frequency and low noise, 3 axis electric field probe, enabling direct ongroundverification by test fornext generation in-situ space plasma sensing missions and for missions with EMC sensitive payload integrated inside the spacecraft structure.DescriptionBackground and Context:Missions that are studying space plasma with wave instruments are imposing low frequency and low-level electric field requirements on the spacecraft in order to limit the unwanted radiated emission that could disturbthe instrument performance. In addition, other increasingly challenging and sensitive payloads also require more stringent control ofelectric fields at lower frequencies. Therefore, the on-ground verification of the electric field requirements driven by the payloads has paramount importance i.e. to confirm the presence of unintentional electric field interference originated from the spacecraftthat can jeopardize the instrument performance. Current electric field probes do not cover the needs of compact probing of low frequency and low noise radiated electric fields in which 3 axes and phase information is needed, in particular to characterise emissions close to units or even inside the spacecraft. By improving both the frequency range and thesensitivity, compact electric field probes could be utilised for improved verification and new applications that were not feasible before.Justification:The commercially available electric field probes are not suitable to capture the low frequencies and the low amplitudes, that are required for upcoming missions of Plasma Observatory, M-Matisse and New ATHENA or required by already flying missions like JUICE and Solar Orbiter.Description:The goal of the activity is to develop a triaxial field probe together with its conditioning unit with start frequency of 0.1 Hz or lower and sensitivity of 0.5 mV/m or lower up-to 200 kHz.An additional constraint for the field probe development is the size. The newly developed field probe shall allow to place minimum of 16 identical field probes around the unit under test at a distance closer than 0.25 m without interfering with each other.Moreover, the field probe needs to produce the field data along eachprincipal axes that can be processed with typical laboratory equipment like spectrum analyser, EMI receiver, digital oscilloscope, data acquisition unit, etc.Task list:- Identification of technology concepts and market research for state-of-the-art field probes in terms of frequency range, sensitivity and dynamic range- Evaluation of weak points of the existing field probes and identification of the critical components needed for the required improvements- Bread boarding of 3 axis sensor (e.g. optimize the type, sizeand shape of sensor) together with its conditioning unit (e.g. design a low noise read out chain including low noise amplifier) also considering constraints like size and cost- Validation tests and reportsDeliverables:- Documentation of the research- The bread board of the improved field probe together with its conditioning unit- Test reports and calibration data

The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. original.description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements.  ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.
